issues.body:
The `gui-bundle` job runs `runs-on: ${{ matrix.os }}` over `ubuntu-latest`, `ubuntu-24.04-arm`, `macos-14`, `macos-15-intel`, `windows-latest`. The new step

    - name: Install Binaryen (wasm-opt)
      run: sudo apt-get update -q && sudo apt-get install -y binaryen

is added with no condition. `apt-get` does not exist on the macOS runners and neither `sudo` nor `apt-get` exists on the Windows runner, so the step fails on all three non-Linux rows. The immediately preceding step in the same job, `Install Tauri system dependencies (Linux)`, does carry `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` — the guard was omitted here.

The macOS/Windows rows are `soft: true` and the job is `continue-on-error: ${{ matrix.soft }}`, so this does NOT fail the release — it silently reports success while skipping the `pkg-gui-<label>` upload. Net effect: every release from now on ships only the Linux installers, and nothing surfaces the regression.

Adding `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` alone does not fix it: the next step is `npm run build:wasm`, and after this PR that script passes `--no-opt` and shells out to `wasm-opt`, so on macOS/Windows the build would then fail at `optimize-wasm.mjs` with 'wasm-opt was not found on PATH'. Previously wasm-pack downloaded its own pinned wasm-opt, so those rows worked without any system package.
issues.fix_hint: Install Binaryen cross-platform in this job rather than via apt. Simplest option: replace the apt step with a Node-based install so it works identically on all five rows, e.g. add `binaryen` as a `js/` devDependency and have `optimize-wasm.mjs` resolve the `wasm-opt` binary from `node_modules/.bin` (falling back to PATH), or use a per-OS step set (`apt-get` on Linux, `brew install binaryen` on macOS, `choco install binaryen` / a pinned GitHub-release download on Windows). Whichever route is chosen, apply it consistently and then re-check every job that runs a `js/` wasm build on a non-Linux runner. Adding a matrix row assertion (fail loudly if `wasm-opt` is absent before the build step) would prevent this class of silent skip.
issues.title: Unguarded `sudo apt-get` added to the 5-OS `gui-bundle` matrix — silently drops the macOS/Windows release installers

issues.body:
All five build scripts now pass `--no-opt` to wasm-pack and delegate optimization to `scripts/optimize-wasm.mjs`, which exits 1 if `wasm-opt` is not on PATH. Before this PR, wasm-pack downloaded and cached its own pinned wasm-opt, so `npm run build:wasm` worked on any platform with only `rustup` + `cargo install wasm-pack`.

This is a breaking change for every downstream consumer of the script, and the fallout is wider than the workflows that were updated:
- `.github/workflows/release.yml` `gui-bundle` on macOS/Windows (see the blocker).
- Local contributors: `js/README.md:71` documents the prerequisites as `rustup target add wasm32-unknown-unknown` + `cargo install wasm-pack`; that list is now incomplete.
- `site/scripts/sync-wasm.mjs:34`, `gui/app/scripts/sync-wasm.mjs:43` and `gui/app/scripts/check-wasm-built.mjs:24` all print `(cd ../js && npm ci && npm run build:wasm)` as the remediation instruction. That instruction now fails on a machine without Binaryen, with an error that does not mention how to install it beyond 'install Binaryen'.

There is no packaged/pinned source of the binary anywhere in the repo, so 'install Binaryen' is left to each environment to solve differently.
issues.fix_hint: Prefer vendoring the optimizer through the existing dependency graph: add `binaryen` (npm) to `js/devDependencies` and have `optimize-wasm.mjs` prefer the locally installed `wasm-opt` before falling back to PATH. That makes `npm ci && npm run build:wasm` self-sufficient on every OS, removes the need for the eight new apt steps entirely, and pins the optimizer version in the lockfile. If PATH-based Binaryen is kept instead, update `js/README.md:71`, the three `sync-wasm`/`check-wasm-built` remediation messages, and `skills/javascript-wasm/SKILL.md` to list it as a required prerequisite with a per-OS install line.
issues.title: `--no-opt` turns Binaryen into an unconditional hard prerequisite for every wasm build, with no cross-platform install path

issues.body:
Eight workflows gain `sudo apt-get update -q && sudo apt-get install -y binaryen` with no version constraint. Two problems:

1. Reproducibility / supply chain. This repo SHA-pins every GitHub Action (`actions/checkout@9c091bb...`, `Swatinem/rust-cache@e18b497...`). The optimizer that now rewrites the bytes actually published to npm (`.github/workflows/publish.yml`) is pulled from a floating distro package whose version changes with the runner image. `wasm-pack`'s bundled wasm-opt was at least a version the wasm-pack release had been tested against; the apt package is typically well behind upstream Binaryen and moves without notice. The artifact is also SLSA-attested downstream, which makes an unpinned transform step more significant, not less.

2. Feature-validation risk that this repo has already hit. `crates/sparq-wasm/Cargo.toml:198-203` documents it explicitly: cargo-level stripping drops the wasm `target_features` custom section 'which wasm-opt reads to auto-enable SIMD / bulk-memory; without it wasm-opt fails validation ("SIMD operations require SIMD")'. The bundle does use SIMD — `scripts/ci-bench.sh` ends with `assert_wasm_simd128`. Auto-enabling from `target_features` requires a reasonably recent Binaryen; whichever version the runner image happens to ship is now load-bearing for the build succeeding at all, on both x64 and `ubuntu-24.04-arm`.

(The step was also duplicated verbatim eight times with the same comment, which makes any future version pin an eight-site edit.)
issues.fix_hint: Pin the optimizer. The cleanest fix is the npm `binaryen` devDependency suggested above — it pins in `package-lock.json`, is cross-platform, and lets all eight apt steps be deleted. If apt is retained, pin the version (`apt-get install -y binaryen=<version>`) or download a specific Binaryen release tarball by tag + checksum, and factor the step into a composite action under `.github/actions/` so there is one place to bump. Also consider asserting a minimum `wasm-opt --version` in `optimize-wasm.mjs` so an old optimizer fails loudly with a clear message rather than at wasm validation.
issues.title: `apt-get install -y binaryen` is unpinned — an unversioned toolchain now transforms the published npm artifact

issues.body:
The PR changes who runs wasm-opt and at what level, but leaves the prose that describes the old behaviour in place. These now actively mislead:

- `crates/sparq-wasm/Cargo.toml:190-196`: 'wasm-opt for `--profile release-wasm` runs wasm-pack's default `-O` (NOT the `release` block's `-Oz`)' and 'wasm-opt `-O` strips + shrinks the shipped `_bg.wasm` on top'. With `--no-opt` wasm-pack now runs no wasm-opt at all, and the level is `-O3`. The same paragraph is repeated near-verbatim in `crates/sparq-reason-wasm/Cargo.toml:63-69`, `crates/sparq-rsp-wasm/Cargo.toml:53-59` and `crates/sparq-text-wasm/Cargo.toml:54-60`.
- The `[package.metadata.wasm-pack.profile.release] wasm-opt = ["-Oz"]` blocks in all four crates were already inert for `--profile release-wasm`; with `--no-opt` they are now unreachable on every path, which is worth stating so a future reader does not 'fix' them.
- `skills/javascript-wasm/SKILL.md:49` still describes `build:wasm` as '(wasm-pack --profile release-wasm + copy)' with no optimize step, and `SKILL.md:429` explains the shipped-bundle optimization story in terms of the wasm-pack pass.

The repo's stated rule is that durable knowledge lives in `AGENTS.md` / `SKILL.md` / crate READMEs and that these stay in sync with the behaviour they describe; `js/README.md` was updated but these were not.
issues.fix_hint: Update the four crates' `[package.metadata.wasm-pack]` comment blocks to state that `js/` now builds with `--no-opt` and applies an explicit pass via `js/scripts/optimize-wasm.mjs` (naming the level per bundle: `-O3` for sparq-wasm, `-Oz` for reason/rsp/text), and note that the `wasm-opt = ["-Oz"]` keys are dead config retained only for a plain `--release` build (or delete them). Update `skills/javascript-wasm/SKILL.md:49` and the optimization paragraph at :429 to match, and add the Binaryen prerequisite to `js/README.md:71`.
issues.title: In-tree comments and SKILL.md documentation describing the wasm-opt behaviour are now false

issues.body:
The README states the main and lean bundles use `-O3` 'where query execution is the priority', and the ci-bench comment adopts the same rationale. No measurement is cited anywhere in the PR — not a browser benchmark, not a `bench/wasm-compare` run. This is a plausible expectation, not an established one; `-O3` over `-O` on wasm-bindgen output does not reliably move query latency, and it reliably increases code size.

The size direction matters because of what is and is not gated. The README correctly notes the hard-gated `wasm_bundle_bytes` ratchet is a raw `cargo build` artifact and is unaffected. The consequence is that the *shipped* bundle — the bytes users actually download — grows with no gate and no ratchet at all; the only signal is the TREND-ONLY `wasm_opt_bundle_bytes` series, whose baseline this same PR redefines (see the ci-bench.sh issue). So the one series that would have shown the regression is reset in the same commit.

This is a claim/evidence gap rather than a correctness defect, but the repo's convention is measure-first for performance changes.
issues.fix_hint: Either attach a measurement (a `bench/wasm-compare/browser` run, or the existing query benchmarks against both bundles) showing `-O3` actually improves query execution enough to justify the size cost, or soften the README wording to state the intent without asserting the outcome. Separately, record the pre/post shipped-bundle size in the PR description so the `wasm_opt_bundle_bytes` step-change is attributable, and consider `-O2` if the measurement shows `-O3` buys size but no speed.
issues.title: The `-O3` switch is justified by an unmeasured performance claim, and grows an unratcheted shipped artifact

issues.body:
Two things in the rewritten comment block:

1. The retained sentence 'The ~10% gap between the two is name-section and producer metadata that browsers strip at load time' was written for `-Oz`. Under `-O3` the post-opt artifact can be the same size as or larger than the raw one (aggressive inlining), so the gap is no longer purely metadata and the stated ~10% no longer holds. The following clause — 'real bundle-size wins from the optimisation program show up here' — is also weaker now that the series measures a speed-first pass.

2. `wasm_opt_bundle_bytes` is a historical trend series. Changing the level from `-Oz` to `-O3` puts a step change in it with nothing recording that pre-change and post-change points are not comparable. Anyone reading the series later will see an unexplained jump.

Minor because the series is explicitly TREND-ONLY and `scripts/perf-gate.py` is correctly left untouched, so nothing is mis-gated.

(Small imprecision too: the new comment says the level matches 'the published main npm bundle', but `WASM_BIN` here is `cargo build -p sparq-wasm` with no features — that is the lean bundle's input, not the main one. The *level* does match both, since `build:wasm:lean` also uses `-O3`, so this is wording only.)
issues.fix_hint: Drop or rewrite the '~10% gap ... metadata' sentence to describe what the -O3 series actually measures. Add one line noting the level changed from -Oz to -O3 in this commit so historical points are not comparable, and reword 'the published main npm bundle' to 'the published engine bundles' since WASM_BIN is the featureless build.
issues.title: Stale explanatory sentence retained after the -Oz → -O3 switch, and the trend series gets an unmarked discontinuity

issues.body:
`--no-opt` was introduced in wasm-pack 0.13.0. CI installs via `cargo install wasm-pack --locked`, which resolves to a recent release, so CI is fine. A contributor with an older wasm-pack already on PATH (0.12.x is still widely installed) gets `error: unexpected argument '--no-opt' found` from all five build scripts, with no hint that the fix is upgrading wasm-pack.

The same applies to `--profile <custom>`, which the scripts already relied on before this PR, so the floor is arguably pre-existing — but `--no-opt` is now the first flag on the command line and will be what fails.
issues.fix_hint: Note the wasm-pack >= 0.13.0 requirement alongside the new Binaryen prerequisite in `js/README.md:71` and `skills/javascript-wasm/SKILL.md`. Optionally have `js/guardrails/prepare-build.mjs` check `wasm-pack --version` and fail with an actionable message, matching the pattern `optimize-wasm.mjs` already uses for the missing-wasm-opt case.
issues.title: `--no-opt` requires wasm-pack >= 0.13.0, with no documented floor

issues.body:
`optimize-wasm.mjs` now sits on the path of every shipped and published wasm artifact, and it overwrites the input in place via `renameSync`. The argument validation and failure cleanup are correct as written, but there is no test for it and no verification of what it produced.

Specifically:
- No check that `wasmPath` exists before invoking; a typo'd path (all five call sites hard-code a long relative path) surfaces as a raw wasm-opt error rather than a clear one.
- No post-condition on the output: the script renames whatever wasm-opt wrote over the original as long as the exit status was 0. A zero-byte or truncated output would be propagated silently into `wasm/` by the subsequent `_copy:wasm`.
- No test coverage. `js/test/` has tests that exercise the built wasm, so a miscompilation would eventually surface, but a build-tooling failure that produces a structurally valid but wrong artifact would not be attributed here.

Minor because the JS test suite, the site/GUI e2e jobs and the Playwright sweeps all run against the optimized bundle, so a broken artifact does get caught somewhere.
issues.fix_hint: Add an `existsSync(wasmPath)` guard with a clear message, and after `spawnSync` succeeds assert the output is non-empty and begins with the `\0asm` magic bytes before renaming. A small `js/test/optimize-wasm.test.mjs` covering the three argument-validation branches (missing path, unsupported level, valid level) would make the contract non-vacuous without needing wasm-opt present.
issues.title: New build-critical script has no test and no post-condition check on its output

verdict.summary:
The change is directionally reasonable (make the wasm-opt pass explicit instead of inheriting wasm-pack's default `-O`, use -O3 for the hot engine bundles and -Oz for the lazy-loaded ones), and the helper script is small and well-behaved (validates the level, cleans up the temp artifact on failure, prints an actionable ENOENT message). The `--no-opt` + explicit-pass ordering is correct, `_copy:wasm` runs after the optimizer, `--config profile.release-wasm.strip=false` is preserved so wasm-opt can still read the `target_features` section, and the hard-gated raw `wasm_bundle_bytes` ratchet is correctly left untouched. CI coverage of the new Binaryen dependency was mostly done carefully: every workflow that runs a `js/` wasm build got the install step, and ci.yml is correctly excluded (it only runs `wasm-pack test`, never `build`).

However there is one blocker. `.github/workflows/release.yml` `gui-bundle` is a five-row OS matrix (ubuntu-latest, ubuntu-24.04-arm, macos-14, macos-15-intel, windows-latest), and the new `Install Binaryen (wasm-opt)` step was added with no `if: runner.os == 'Linux'` guard — unlike the adjacent `Install Tauri system dependencies (Linux)` step in the same job, which is guarded. `sudo apt-get` does not exist on the macOS or Windows runners, so those three rows now fail at that step. Because they are `soft: true` / `continue-on-error`, the failure is silent: every release will simply stop shipping the macOS and Windows desktop installers. Merely adding an `if: Linux` guard is not sufficient either — the very next step runs `npm run build:wasm`, which now hard-requires `wasm-opt` on PATH, so those rows need a genuine cross-platform Binaryen install.

Secondary concerns: the apt package is unpinned (version drift on a published artifact in a repo that SHA-pins every action), and several in-tree comments/docs describing the old wasm-pack-runs-wasm-opt behaviour are now false.
